    ineligibility reason `B4 HeuristicPublicControl 0.4844 < 0.5000`.
  - Warning emitted: `no B1 candidate met the required anchor threshold`.

### Additional Failed Ideas Recorded

- Allow-main-move eval on the teacherfade update-50 checkpoint:
  B4/control dropped to `55/128 = 0.4296875`. The existing main-move guard is
  masking a real weakness, but simply allowing movement makes the policy worse.
- B4 exact-family intervention
  (`main_guided_factorized_postbest_b4exact_from_teacherfade50_u25_20260515`):
  periodic update 25 aggregate `0.609375`, B0 `1.0`, B2 `0.5625`,
  B3 `0.46875`, B4 `0.40625`. Auxiliary metrics moved, but policy quality
  degraded, so broad exact-family pressure is not a good B1-local fix as
  configured.

### Tests and Validation

- `uv run --extra dev python -m pytest -q python/weiss_rl/tests/test_b1_candidate_selection.py`
  passed (`7 passed`).
- `uv run --extra dev ruff check python/weiss_rl/experiments/b1_candidate_selection.py python/weiss_rl/tests/test_b1_candidate_selection.py`
  passed (`All checks passed!`).

### Findings

- The candidate-selection workflow was under-optimized and structurally unsafe:
  it could select stale/imported seed snapshots and ignore stronger targeted
  confirmation evidence.
- After repairing that workflow, no currently tested B1/guided-bootstrap
  checkpoint passes the strict B2/B3/B4 `>= 0.5` confirmed-anchor gate.
- Teacherfade update 50 remains the best confirmed checkpoint by 128-paired
  aggregate and B2/B3 strength, but it is still just short on B4/control:
  B4 `124/256 = 0.484375`.
- The repeated B4 misses across teacherfade, strong-anchor, profile-floor,
  top-action anchor, and B4-exact probes make this look less like ordinary
  training noise and more like a structural limitation of the isolated B1
  setup or current B4-control action surface.

### Remaining Risks

- A 64-paired local eval can still look eligible and then fail at 128 paired
  seeds. Do not promote a B1 candidate from 16- or 64-paired evidence alone.
- The selector now makes the failure visible, but it does not make the policy
  better. It should be treated as workflow repair plus evidence consolidation.
- Guided B1 can be described as a strong bootstrap candidate only with an
  explicit caveat that B4/control remains below the confirmed threshold.

### Next Action

Stop spending broad B1-local probes unless they directly target the B4/control
mechanism with a new structural idea. The evidence now supports either:

1. pivoting to the full thesis league model, where B3/B4/control pressure is
   part of the actual training distribution; or
2. building a narrower B4-control state/action replay intervention for
   `main_move` and exact within-family choices before any more B1 training.

The safest thesis workflow is now: keep `latest` as latest, keep `best` as the
best confirmed checkpoint, do not publish `b1_noleague_baseline` from guided
runs, and use `diagnostics/b1_candidate_selection_20260515.json` as the
machine-readable evidence that B1 has not yet cleared the strict confirmed
B2/B3/B4 gate.

  - Command: `uv run --extra dev python python/scripts/learning_progress_diagnostic.py --run-dir runs/main_guided_factorized_liveleague_from_teacherfade50_u50_20260515 --league-guard --guard-max-vtrace-rho-p99 25`
  - Expected result: exited nonzero after writing
    `diagnostics/learning_progress_summary.json`.
  - Failures: B2 latest anchor `0.34375 < 0.45`,
    B3 latest anchor `0.40625 < 0.45`, no promotion pass after `9` attempts,
    `9` consecutive promotion failures, and `vtrace_rho_p99`
    `29.6266 > 25`.
  - CLI command: `uv run --extra dev python -m weiss_rl.cli guard-run --run-dir runs/main_guided_factorized_liveleague_from_teacherfade50_u50_20260515 --max-vtrace-rho-p99 25`
  - Expected result: same nonzero guard failure, without a traceback.
- Candidate selection:
  - Command: re-ran `select_b1_candidate.py` with the live-league run included.
  - Result: selected checkpoint remains the intentionally ineligible
    teacherfade update-50 candidate; no B1 candidate met the strict confirmed
    anchor threshold.

### Findings

- Early live PFSP/promotion does not fix the post-50 collapse. In this local
  shape it made B2/B3/B4 worse immediately and never promoted a checkpoint.
- The "just turn the league on sooner" hypothesis is now weak. The promotion
  gate is doing useful work by refusing bad checkpoints, but the training
  distribution still drifts away from the anchor set.
- The large live-league V-trace tails are a stronger structural lead than
  another reward-shaping tweak. League routing introduces heavier off-policy
  correction tails, while train-filtered rows can still look numerically
  tame.

### Next Action

Before any full thesis league production run, add a guarded league launch path
that fails fast when early promotion gates all fail or when B2/B3/B4 periodic
anchors collapse. The next technical hypothesis should target live-league
off-policy/routing pressure: either reduce early opponent-policy staleness,
separate train/eval rows more explicitly in diagnostics, or keep the full
league warmup longer but require confirmation before extending past the first
50-100 updates.

    second falloff warning and did not satisfy the strict anchor gate.

### Findings

- Adding B3/B4 variant pressure did not fix the isolated continuation. It
  shifted the tradeoff: B4 reached `0.5` in the noisy update-50 periodic eval,
  but B2 and B3 both fell to `0.40625`.
- The proxy mismatch persists. Teacher/action auxiliary metrics can improve
  while B2/B3/B4 anchor outcomes degrade.
- This makes a full thesis league run from the current teacherfade checkpoint
  risky unless the next run changes the objective or sampling balance more
  deliberately than simply adding B3/B4 variants.

### Next Action

Do not promote this variant-profile probe. The next high-value move is to
prepare the full thesis league run as a guarded experiment, not as a thesis
production launch: start from the teacherfade update-50 checkpoint, keep B1
baseline import disabled or clearly labeled as guided-bootstrap, and add early
candidate selection/confirmation gates so a B2/B3 collapse is caught around the
first 25-50 updates instead of after a long run.

  `test_config_loader.py` cover live mirror sampling and metrics.

  main-move-only filtering.

  `test_config_loader.py` cover
  `training.action_surface.main_move_only_max_consecutive`.
- Canonical structured-acceptance config hashes were refreshed after the new
  canonical action-surface field.
- Validation:
  - `uv run --extra dev python -m pytest -q python/weiss_rl/tests/test_runtime_action_surface.py python/weiss_rl/tests/test_config_sections_training.py python/weiss_rl/tests/test_runtime_config.py python/weiss_rl/tests/test_config_loader.py::test_load_stack_config_supports_guided_factorized_postbest_mainmove_once_probe`
    passed (`16 passed`).
  - `uv run --extra dev python -m pytest -q python/weiss_rl/tests/test_config_loader.py::test_structured_acceptance_public_preset_canonical_hashes_are_pinned python/weiss_rl/tests/test_runtime_action_surface.py python/weiss_rl/tests/test_config_sections_training.py python/weiss_rl/tests/test_runtime_config.py python/weiss_rl/tests/test_config_loader.py::test_load_stack_config_supports_guided_factorized_postbest_mainmove_once_probe python/weiss_rl/tests/test_config_loader.py::test_load_stack_config_supports_guided_factorized_liveleague_mirror_probe`
    passed (`21 passed`).
  - Targeted ruff check on touched config/runtime/eval/test files reported
    `All checks passed!`.

### Findings

- The seed-snapshot chronology bug was real and fixed, but it was not the
  main quality bottleneck.
- The no-mirror liveleague failure was structural: PFSP readiness removed the
  mirror lane and left only about half the batch training the focal policy.
- Keeping an explicit mirror lane improves liveleague health:
  policy-train fraction rises to roughly `0.68-0.71`, train-row V-trace tails
  stay tame, and B2 remains stronger than the no-mirror liveleague run.
- Mirror liveleague still does not solve B3/B4/control. Its 128-paired
  confirmation is worse than teacherfade update 50, especially on B3/B4.
- B4/control remains an exact within-family action problem. The mirror audit
  has the same shape as teacherfade/profile-floor: high family agreement but
  weak exact choices inside attack, main-play-character, and clock-from-hand.
- Main-move is a visible B4 mismatch, but relaxing the guard is not sufficient.
  The policy has not learned good movement, so allowing one movement still
  hurts B4.

### Behavior Changes

- Future seed-pool imports no longer pollute local snapshot chronology.
- Future liveleague configs can retain a scheduled mirror/self-play lane after
  PFSP readiness.
- `latest`, `best`, and `observed_best` semantics remain separated and were
  verified on the mirror liveleague run.
- The main-move-only guard can now be tuned without editing code, but the first
  probe shows the current policy should not use the relaxed setting for thesis
  candidate selection.

### Remaining Risks

- No strict B1/guided-bootstrap checkpoint currently passes the confirmed
  B2/B3/B4 `>= 0.5` gate.
- Teacherfade update 50 remains the best confirmed candidate by aggregate
  and B2/B3 strength, but B4/control remains just below threshold.
- Liveleague mirror routing is healthier but not a policy-quality solution.
- Further isolated B1 probes are now likely to burn time unless they introduce
  a genuinely new B4-state/action mechanism.

### Next Action

Stop broad B1-local probing. The evidence now supports a guarded full-league
pivot rather than another isolated continuation tweak: start from teacherfade
update 50, keep the mirror lane, keep seed imports at local update `0`, require
early B2/B3/B4 confirmation around updates `25-50`, and treat
`diagnostics/b1_candidate_selection_20260515.json` as the machine-readable
record that the strict B1 gate is not yet cleared.

### Behavior Changes

- The evidence-backed guided-bootstrap route no longer depends on a hand-built
  `python/scripts/train.py` command.
- The `league-probe` profile now uses process collection by default, because
  central collection is dominated by fixed/model opponent routing in this league
  workload.
- B3/B4 heuristic opponents are no longer accidentally routed through the B2
  native base heuristic when the native fixed-opponent backend is active.
- `latest`, `best`, and `observed_best` checkpoint semantics are unchanged.
  The new command only changes how the bootstrap run is launched.

### Remaining Risks

- This is workflow plumbing, not new model-quality evidence.
- The guided-bootstrap path still needs an early 25-50 update run with
  `guard-run`, targeted B2/B3/B4 confirmation, and candidate selection before
  it can be treated as a thesis candidate.
- Simulator-native aggressive/control profile actions did not match the RL
  Python oracle in an exploratory parity check, so B3/B4 native profile routing
  is intentionally disabled in the RL repo until that contract is reconciled.
- Process collection improves guided-bootstrap throughput, but at about
  `8.5k` samples/sec for a 2-update smoke it is still materially slower than
  B1 no-league. Further performance work should batch model-opponent rows or
  reduce fixed-opponent routing overhead.

### Next Action

Run the focused workflow tests, ruff, and a dry-run plan artifact. If those are
green, launch a short CLI smoke/probe only to validate plumbing before any
longer thesis-local guided-bootstrap run.

### Tests

- `uv run --extra dev python -m pytest -q python/weiss_rl/tests/test_config_loader.py::test_load_stack_config_supports_guided_factorized_postbest_vtrace_profile_floor_probe python/weiss_rl/tests/test_config_loader.py::test_load_stack_config_supports_guided_factorized_postbest_vtrace_variant005_probe python/weiss_rl/tests/test_config_loader.py::test_load_stack_config_supports_guided_factorized_postbest_vtrace_control_floor_probe`
  passed (`3 passed`).
- `uv run --extra dev ruff check python/weiss_rl/tests/test_config_loader.py`
  reported `All checks passed!`.
- Earlier attempted `ruff check` over the YAML config plus Python test failed
  because Ruff parsed the YAML file as Python; this is not a repo failure and
  should not be used as a validation command for YAML configs.

### Findings

- The process-backed guided-bootstrap path fixed workflow and throughput, but
  did not improve quality over the previous best teacherfade/vtrace candidates.
- The B4 problem is not primarily broad family selection. The learner usually
  chooses the right family but the wrong exact card, slot, attack target, or
  movement action.
- Conservative V-trace clipping remains the most promising structural change:
  it produced the closest complete B2/B3/B4 confirm (`B4 125/256`), and its
  B4-only confirm256 stayed close but below parity.
- Small direct B3/B4 variant exposure and control-profile teacher floors look
  good on tiny periodic evals but fail under 128-paired confirmation.
- The checkpoint guard is doing useful work: the `vtrace_variant005` extension
  to update 50 collapsed, and `best` stayed on update 25 while `latest` stayed
  chronological at update 50.
- B4/control is a stronger/different anchor than B2-base. B2 loses to B4 at
  `121/256`, so a strict B1 > 0.5 B4 threshold is a stronger condition than
  "beat the B2 heuristic baseline."

### Remaining Risks

- No candidate currently clears B2/B3/B4 at `>= 0.5` under 128 paired seeds.
- Tiny periodic dev eval frequently overestimates B4, so it must not drive
  promotion alone.
- B4 exact-action weakness may need a better action-argument objective or
  offline/public-teacher pretraining; simply cycling profiles or adding small
  variant opponent lanes has not solved it.
- The strongest teacherfade candidate is close to B4 parity but still below it
  at 256 paired seeds.

### Next Action

Stop treating "train longer" as the next default. The next useful branch is a
structural exact-action intervention: either improve factorized argument
supervision for B4-sensitive rows (`main_play_character`, `clock_from_hand`,
`attack`, and movement) or build a short supervised public-heuristic pretrain
stage, then rerun the 25-update V-trace-clamped post-best probe. In parallel,
update candidate selection/reporting to show anchor-vs-anchor reference scores
so thesis gating can distinguish "below parity vs B4" from "worse than B2."

### Findings

- The top B1/guided candidate is not thesis-eligible under the strict
  B2/B3/B4 `>= 0.5` confirmed gate.
- It is also not "worse than B2": on the common B3/B4 anchors, the selected
  teacherfade candidate beats B2's own reference results, including a small
  B4/control edge.
- This supports a thesis framing where the current B1 is a useful guided
  bootstrap candidate but not a clean final B1 baseline.
- The reference parser initially treated numeric targeted-confirm metadata as
  scores. That was fixed by preferring `anchor_scores`, then matchup `rows`,
  and only then a direct score mapping.

### Remaining Risks

- The reference comparison is diagnostic only. It must not be used to publish
  `b1_noleague_baseline`, because the selected candidate still fails the
  strict B4 parity gate.
- B4 remains the blocker for a clean B1. The strongest candidates now separate
  into "beats B2 reference" and "clears parity"; only the first is true.

### Next Action

Use `diagnostics/b1_candidate_selection_20260515_reference_b2.json` as the
machine-readable closeout for the current B1-local search. Unless a genuinely
new structural B4 intervention appears, pivot effort to the full thesis league
path and carry forward teacherfade/V-trace as bootstrap evidence rather than
pretending B1 has cleared strict parity.

  - Command: `PYTHONHASHSEED=0 uv run --extra dev --extra sim python python/scripts/b2_disagreement_audit.py --stack-config configs/thesis/main_league_guided_bootstrap_seedchampion.yaml --run-dir runs/main_guided_bootstrap_seedchampion_league_probe_process_20260515 --snapshot-registry-json runs/main_guided_bootstrap_seedchampion_league_probe_process_20260515/training/snapshots/registry.json --output-run-dir diagnostics/audit_seedchampion_u50_vs_B4_20260515_legaldiag --episodes-jsonl runs/main_guided_bootstrap_seedchampion_league_probe_process_20260515/eval/targeted_confirm128_policy_000010/matchups/00_policy_000010__vs__04_b4_heuristicpubliccontrol/episodes.jsonl --policy-id policy_000010 --opponent-policy-id "B4 HeuristicPublicControl" --summary-json diagnostics/audit_seedchampion_u50_vs_B4_20260515_legaldiag/summary.json --top-k 30 --top-actions 5`
  - Reran `256` games across `128` paired seeds, compared `42480` steps,
    and inspected `7680` top-difference rows.
  - Overall top-action match vs B4 top action: `0.620951`; top-family match:
    `0.969115`.
  - Model-facing legal surface filter rate: `0.284581`; heuristic/B4 filter
    rate: `0.0`.
  - B4 top action illegal for the model rate: `0.024882`.
  - Raw legal count mean: `7.9909`; model legal count mean: `6.4457`; B4
    legal count mean: `7.9909`.
  - B4 top-family exact rates: attack `0.4355`, main-play-character
    `0.3313`, clock-from-hand `0.3453`, main-move `0.0`.
  - For B4 `main_move` top rows (`1057` compared decisions), the heuristic
    top action was legal for the model `0.0` of the time, confirming these are
    intentionally filtered by the model action-surface guard.

### Findings

- Conservative V-trace clipping is not the missing fix. It made train-row
  correction tails easier to interpret, but did not improve B2/B3/B4 quality.
- The league is not frozen merely because the strict promotion gate fails.
  The process guided-bootstrap run already sampled probationary recent
  snapshots heavily, and the seed-champion run successfully sampled imported
  seed snapshots as a champion lane.
- Marking imported seed snapshots as training champions improves the mechanics
  and keeps a stable champion lane alive, but it does not solve B4/control.
- The strongest confirmed candidate is still teacherfade update 50. Seed
  championing is a useful negative result, not a better B1.
- The B4 `main_move` mismatch is real and now quantified, but it is not the
  dominant explanation for B4 weakness: B4's top action is illegal for the
  model on only `2.49%` of compared decisions, while exact action choice inside
  legal attack, main-play-character, and clock-from-hand rows remains weak.
- The main-move guard should remain treated as an action-surface abstraction,
  not a hidden bug. Prior raw/one-shot main-move probes worsened B4, and the
  refreshed audit shows the larger problem is still exact within-family
  selection.

### Behavior Changes

- Guided-bootstrap can now explicitly choose one of three bootstrap stacks:
  normal, V-trace-clamped, or seed-champion.
- Imported seed snapshots can be promoted into the training champion pool by
  config, while promotion-gate artifacts remain the only thesis champion
  signal.
- `guard-run` artifacts now explain whether large V-trace tails are on train
  rows or filtered/non-train rows, and whether champion sampling is imported
  bootstrap pressure or promotion-gate admission.
- Disagreement audits now make model-only legal-surface filtering visible at
  summary level, so future B2/B3/B4 audits no longer require digging through
  giant per-step examples to notice action-surface mismatches.

### Remaining Risks

- No B1/guided-bootstrap candidate clears strict confirm128 B2/B3/B4 parity.
- B4 remains the hard blocker and is still an exact within-family action
  issue, not a broad league-pool issue.
- The seed-champion stack should stay as a diagnostic/bootstrap option, not a
  default thesis path, unless later full-league evidence says it improves main
  model stability.

### Next Action

Do not keep trying small isolated B1 knobs. The current evidence closes the
league-freeze hypothesis: adaptive/recent sampling and seed champion sampling
both work, but neither fixes B4. Continue with the guarded full-league pivot
from teacherfade update 50, preserve early B2/B3/B4 guard checks, and use the
candidate-selection artifacts to state honestly that strict B1 parity is not
cleared.

### Findings

- This is the first guided-bootstrap candidate in the current search that
  clears B2/B3/B4 at complete 256-paired-seed confirmation.
- The run still is not monotonic. `latest.pt` correctly remains chronological
  at update `100`, and that latest policy fails B4 badly under confirm128.
  The usable candidate is update `90`, not latest.
- The previous selector was a real workflow problem: it could miss a confirmed
  checkpoint if the checkpoint came between periodic dev-eval rows. That would
  have made this run look like another failure even though update `90` was
  thesis-relevant.
- The update-90 policy wins B4 despite not matching B4's exact top action
  better than earlier near-misses. Compared with the earlier seed-champion B4
  audit, top-action/family agreement is lower, so the improvement is likely
  game-outcome robustness from the longer guided league dynamics rather than
  direct B4 imitation.

### Behavior Changes

- Candidate selection now includes complete targeted-confirm-only snapshots
  from the registry. These candidates are marked with
  `targeted_confirm_only: true` and keep their real update, snapshot path, and
  weights hash.
- `select_b1_candidate.py --publish-selected-alias` can now pin a chosen
  guided/bootstrap candidate under a neutral policy id such as
  `guided_bootstrap_selected`, avoiding fragile manual policy-id copy/paste.
- This preserves `latest.pt` and strict `best.pt` semantics: the selector
  surfaces update `90` as a selected candidate artifact without rewriting
  chronological latest or pretending the strict promotion gate passed.

### Remaining Risks

- This is an eligible guided-bootstrap candidate, not a pure B1 NoLeague
  baseline. It should be described as the justified guided-league bootstrap
  candidate unless a pure B1 clears the same standard later.
- Update `100` falls off, so the underlying non-monotonicity is not solved.
  We have a usable selected checkpoint, but not a training process that can be
  trusted to make the latest checkpoint good automatically.
- The strict league promotion gate still never passed. It may be too strict for
  this noisy local regime, or it may be guarding against real anchor tradeoffs;
  do not bypass it without a separate promotion-gate audit.

### Next Action

Promote the selector artifact, not `latest.pt`, as the current guided-bootstrap
candidate. Next, remove the remaining manual step by adding a generic
non-baseline selected-candidate alias/export path, then run the same confirm256
selector on any full thesis league continuation. If training is continued from
update `90`, use `policy_000018` weights explicitly and keep early B4 guard
checks, because update `100` is already known to be worse.

  - passed: `15 passed`.

  - reported `All checks passed!`.

### Findings

- The selected-checkpoint path had two structural problems:
  - fresh init needed schedule offset so teacher/public guidance did not restart;
  - resume needed to persist the same offset, otherwise a resumed run silently
    replayed early guidance time.
- Policy anchoring must be explicitly refreshed after external checkpoint
  initialization. The default lazy anchor was probably safe in the current
  direct path, but the new reset hook removes the ambiguity and protects future
  callers.
- KL anchor alone is not enough. The best clean branch requires a small
  explicit public-heuristic floor (`0.04`) plus KL anchor.
- The best current artifact is no longer the original update-90 alias. The
  better selected candidate is
  `runs/main_guided_bootstrap_selected_anchor_floor_u25_20260516`
  `guided_bootstrap_floor_selected` / `policy_000005` / update `25`.
- Non-monotonicity is still real. The public-floor run improves the candidate,
  but update `50` is worse than update `25`; the guard correctly rolls back and
  the selector pins the selected candidate instead of relying on latest.

### Remaining Risks

- This is still a guided/bootstrap candidate, not a pure B1 NoLeague baseline.
- The latest checkpoint is not thesis-usable. Use the pinned selected alias or
  `best.pt`, not chronological `latest.pt`.
- Confirmation is `128` paired seeds, not `256`; the candidate is promising and
  better than the prior selected checkpoint on overall/B3/B4, but a final
  thesis claim should still use confirm256/final matrix.
- The core "keeps improving indefinitely" problem is not solved. What is solved
  is: the workflow can now detect falloff, preserve a better selected candidate,
  and avoid manual policy-id selection.

### Next Action

Treat `guided_bootstrap_floor_selected` as the current best guided-bootstrap B1
candidate. Next, either run confirm256 on that alias or use it as the seed for
the full thesis league path with early B2/B3/B4 guard checks. If continuing to
search B1-only improvements, prioritize structural anti-drift mechanisms such
as segmented train-eval-reanchor loops or adaptive early stop on B3/B4 decline;
lower LR and profile cycling did not solve the drift.

    offset and the focused checkpoint tests passed.

  - plus focused checkpoint/minimal-loop tests.

  - `python/weiss_rl/experiments/segmented_b1_guided_bootstrap.py`
  - `python/scripts/segmented_b1_guided_bootstrap.py`
  - `python/weiss_rl/cli.py`
  - warm-start/checkpoint/tests touched in this milestone.

### Findings

- The earlier selected-continuation attempts had a second schedule-time bug:
  continuing from a derived checkpoint reset effective guidance time from
  `90 + 25` down to `25`. This likely explains at least part of the lower-LR
  continuation failure from the public-floor candidate.
- The segmented controller now gives a concrete anti-drift path:
  - segment 1 improved the selected candidate;
  - segment 2 detected degradation and stopped automatically.
- Periodic 16-pair dev eval is too noisy to be the sole selection signal:
  segment 1 periodic B3 was `0.375`, while confirm64/128/256 all cleared B3.
  The workflow should continue to use periodic dev eval as a cheap trigger and
  targeted confirmation as the selection signal.
- Current best guided/bootstrap B1 candidate:
  - run:
    `runs/b1_guided_floor_segmented_effoffset_u25_confirm64_20260516_seg01`
  - alias: `guided_bootstrap_floor_segmented_selected`
  - update: `25`
  - confirm256 overall: `0.685546875`
  - confirm256 B2/B3/B4: `0.59375`, `0.546875`, `0.6015625`
  - selector artifact:
    `diagnostics/b1_candidate_selection_guided_floor_segmented_confirm256_20260516.json`
- Compared with the previous `guided_bootstrap_floor_selected` confirm256,
  the new candidate improves overall, B2, and B4, but gives up B3.

### Remaining Risks

- The new candidate is still a guided/bootstrap B1, not a pure B1 NoLeague
  model.
- B3 is now the weakest confirmed row at `0.546875`; it is above threshold but
  not large-margin.
- Segment 2 confirms that more segmented continuation is not automatically
  better. The controller stopped correctly, but the learning process still does
  not monotonically improve.
- Promotion gate still fails on these local segments. Treat the segmented alias
  as a selected bootstrap artifact, not a strict promoted league champion.

### Next Action

Use `guided_bootstrap_floor_segmented_selected` as the current best
guided-bootstrap B1 seed. Next, either:

1. run the guarded full thesis league bootstrap from this alias with early
   B2/B3/B4 guard checks, or
2. test one targeted B3-preserving variant, since B3 is the only confirmed
   regression versus the previous public-floor candidate.

### Findings

- Current best B1-guided seed remains:
  - `runs/b1_guided_floor_segmented_effoffset_u25_confirm64_20260516_seg01`
  - alias `guided_bootstrap_floor_segmented_selected`
  - confirm256 B2/B3/B4: `0.59375`, `0.546875`, `0.6015625`
- Main-league transfer from that seed is the fragile part, not the seed
  snapshot itself:
  - the imported seed inside the first transfer run beat B4 at
    `79/128 = 0.6171875`;
  - B4 regressed after main-league updates.
- The B4/control collapse is not fixed by simply increasing KL anchor strength:
  anchor `0.20` improved the update-10 B4 gate to exactly `0.5`, but update 25
  still fell to `0.45703125`.
- The B4/control collapse is also not fixed by adding a persistent control-only
  public heuristic floor with conservative V-trace clipping. That variant hit
  `0.4453125` at update 10.
- Periodic dev eval remains too optimistic/noisy for checkpoint selection:
  the anchor `0.20` 25-update run had periodic aggregate `0.609375` and
  confirmatory aggregate `0.59375`, but targeted B4 confirm128 was below
  threshold.

### Remaining Risks

- The guided seed is useful, but the main-league continuation objective still
  has a structural B4/control retention problem.
- B4 failure may be caused by action-family or within-family preference drift
  under league batches rather than by missing control-profile supervision.
- The public-teacher floor may be misaligned with B4 in the states that matter
  for control matchups; the control-only floor result makes this especially
  suspicious.
- The all-row targeted confirm helper still trips over canonical B1 alias
  resolution for transfer runs; use explicit B0/B2/B3/B4 targeted calls or
  improve the helper before relying on all-row output there.

### Next Action

- Do not promote any main-league transfer checkpoint from the anchor `0.08`,
  anchor `0.20`, or vtrace-control-floor branches.
- Keep `guided_bootstrap_floor_segmented_selected` as the current best
  selected B1 seed.
- Next structural diagnosis should compare the selected seed versus failed
  transfer checkpoints on the same B4/control public states:
  - family choice drift,
  - same-family action choice drift,
  - pass/nonpass and attack-type decisions,
  - public heuristic target agreement,
  - value/reward advantage signs on the differing decisions.
- If running another training probe before that diagnosis, prefer a
  B4-sensitive exact-action or same-family-margin variant over more anchor or
  public-floor pressure.

      `0.817047817047817`, family match `1.0`
- Coarse B4 trajectory/action counters:

    - pass actions per game `30.458984375`
    - pass-with-nonpass-available per game `10.728515625`
    - main-move actions per game `2.580078125`
  - failed anchor `0.20` transfer confirm128 vs B4:
    - B4 mean `117/256 = 0.45703125`
    - pass actions per game `31.55859375`
    - pass-with-nonpass-available per game `12.359375`
    - main-move actions per game `2.3203125`
  - B4-exact update-10 confirm64 vs B4:
    - B4 mean `57/128 = 0.4453125`
    - pass actions per game `30.4140625`
    - pass-with-nonpass-available per game `10.953125`
    - main-move actions per game `2.3984375`
- B4-exact anchor `0.20` update 10:
  - run:
    `runs/main_league_from_segmented_selected_b4exact_anchor020_u10_20260516`
  - update 10 scalar:
    - `guidance_schedule_update_count=150`
    - `init_schedule_offset_updates=140`
    - `policy_anchor_coef_active=0.2`
    - `policy_anchor_kl_mean=0.05766484513878822`
    - `teacher_supervised_coef_scale_active=0.5`
    - `teacher_clock_from_hand_accuracy=0.42232025754143315`
    - `teacher_same_family_action_accuracy=0.43511858276131365`
    - `throughput_samples_per_sec=7564.79488785058`
  - B4-only confirm64:
    - `57/128 = 0.4453125`

### Findings

- The selected seed remains better than the failed transfer against B4, but on
  the failed transfer's own replay states the seed is only modestly more
  B4-aligned overall:
  - top-action match `0.6546` vs `0.6364`
  - probability on B4 top action `0.5316` vs `0.5219`
- The clearest same-state regression is clocking:
  - selected seed vs B4 clock_from_hand top-action match: `0.4933`
  - failed transfer vs B4 clock_from_hand top-action match: `0.2780`
  - failed transfer also sometimes leaves the clock_from_hand family when the
    seed/B4 comparison stays in-family.
- Main-play-character is mostly same-family but weak exact choice in both seed
  and failed transfer on the failed-transfer states. The failed transfer puts
  slightly less probability on B4's top main-play-character action, but the
  difference is not large enough to explain the whole B4 win-rate collapse.
- Stronger exact/same-family B4-sensitive auxiliary pressure did not fix the
  B4 gate. The B4-exact branch failed at update 10 with the same `57/128`
  result as the control-floor branch.
- The B4 collapse is therefore unlikely to be solved by simply adding more
  public-teacher floor, more control-profile labels, or stronger exact-action
  auxiliary loss on the obvious B4-sensitive families.
- The remaining likely cause is trajectory-distribution drift or credit
  assignment under league updates:
  - failed transfer enters states where even the selected seed is only
    marginally better locally;
  - the selected seed's own B4 eval remains much stronger.

### Remaining Risks

- The same-state audit used a 16-paired-seed slice from the failed transfer's
  B4 confirm128, not a full confirm-sized replay audit.
- Replay-state comparisons are observational: they explain local policy
  differences on recorded trajectories, but not counterfactual outcome changes
  when another policy would have entered a different state.
- B4-exact was only tested for 10 updates because it failed the early B4 gate.
  Extending it would likely be wasted unless another diagnostic contradicts the
  early result.

### Next Action

- Do not extend the B4-exact, control-floor, or anchor-only transfer branches.
- Next high-value diagnostic is trajectory-distribution comparison between the
  selected seed and failed transfer on paired B4 evals:
  - phase/level/damage/stock/hand/board distributions before focal decisions,
  - outcome-conditioned clock_from_hand and pass-with-nonpass states,
  - early-game divergence points before the failed transfer enters bad control
    trajectories.
- If training again before that diagnosis, use a conservative continuation
  that preserves the selected seed's trajectory distribution, such as frozen or
  heavily KL-constrained early league updates, rather than stronger public
  teacher labels.

- Stronger anchoring can partially retain B4, but it does not solve balanced
  B2/B3/B4 transfer. The B3 drop in the strong-KL probe is a hard reject.
- The new trajectory comparison confirms why global KL and top-action metrics
  were misleading: small same-state distribution differences can accumulate
  into different game trajectories with fewer useful non-pass actions and lower
  board presence.
- The main league continuation problem is now better described as
  trajectory-retention/credit-assignment fragility, not just public-teacher
  mismatch or weak anchor strength.

### Remaining Risks

- The same-seed trajectory comparison uses 16 paired seeds from a B4 slice. It
  is strong diagnostic evidence, but not thesis-grade final eval evidence.
- Strong KL was tested only to update 10 because B3 already failed; extending
  it would likely waste compute unless a new B3-specific structural change is
  introduced.
- The current selected seed is good enough to keep as the B1/guided-bootstrap
  candidate, but the full league model still needs a transfer/training design
  that does not erode B3 or B4.

### Next Action

- Do not promote the top-action or strong-KL selected-seed transfer probes.
- Keep `guided_bootstrap_floor_segmented_selected` as current best.
- Use the new trajectory comparison tooling for any future B3/B4 transfer
  branch; require retained B2/B3/B4 confirm performance and no passivity/board
  regression before extending.
- Next structural training direction should be a trajectory-retention design,
  not another public-teacher or global-KL-only variant:
  - freeze/import selected seed as a non-updated champion for the main league,
    while training a separate learner;
  - or add an explicit early-update guard that stops/reverts when B3/B4 or
    trajectory metrics regress;
  - or collect targeted B3/B4 counterfactual data and train a small retention
    objective on the earliest divergent decisions.

## 2026-05-16 - Guarded League Bootstrap Controller

### What Changed

- Added `python/weiss_rl/experiments/guarded_league_bootstrap.py`, a short-segment
  guided-league controller that:
  - trains from an explicit seed checkpoint for a small update segment;
  - resolves the latest chronological `policy_...` snapshot from the segment;
  - runs targeted confirm eval against B2/B3/B4;
  - advances the source checkpoint only if the latest segment checkpoint passes
    the guard;
  - stops immediately on missing anchors, scores below threshold, or excessive
    drop versus a reference summary.
- Added CLI/script surfaces:
  - `python/scripts/guarded_league_bootstrap.py`
  - `python -m weiss_rl.cli guarded-league-bootstrap`
- Added `python/weiss_rl/tests/test_guarded_league_bootstrap.py`.
- Extended `python/weiss_rl/tests/test_cli_workflow.py` so the standard thesis
  CLI exposes the guarded controller.

### Behavior Changes

- Best/latest semantics are kept separate. The controller does not repoint a
  best alias to latest. It only uses latest as the candidate for the current
  segment and refuses to carry it forward unless it passes B2/B3/B4 guards.
- A rejected segment leaves the previous source checkpoint as the last accepted
  continuation point.
- The default guard uses B2, B3, and B4 with:
  - `min_required_anchor_score=0.5`
  - `max_reference_drop=0.04` when a reference summary is supplied

  - B3 `0.546875`
  - B4 `0.6015625`

### Tests Added

- Latest snapshot resolution ignores imported seed aliases and requires a
  matching checkpoint.
- Guard decision rejects below-threshold anchors and excessive reference drops.
- Dry-run writes a segment plan plus confirm-command template.
- Fake-runner integration stops after a failing B3 guard and does not start a
  second segment.
- Fake-runner integration advances the source checkpoint only after all anchors
  pass.
- CLI dry-run wraps the controller with the selected-seed reference summary.

### Findings

- The next real league transfer should be a guarded short-segment run, not a
  half-day continuation. Prior probes show that useful-looking losses or anchor
  metrics can coexist with B3/B4 erosion.
- The guard operationalizes the current selection evidence: the selected seed is
  the reference, and every proposed latest continuation must retain B2/B3/B4
  before it becomes the next source checkpoint.

### Remaining Risks

- The guarded controller prevents wasting compute on already-failed latest
  checkpoints, but it does not by itself solve the underlying trajectory
  retention problem.
- Confirm64 is still a local gating budget, not final thesis evidence.
- A segment can pass B2/B3/B4 while still drifting in trajectory metrics; if this
  happens, add trajectory-summary gates from the B4 comparison tooling.

### Next Action

- Run the real guarded selected-seed league probe for one 10-update segment.
- If it passes B2/B3/B4 relative to the selected-seed reference, continue one
  more guarded segment.
- If it fails, keep the selected seed as the best B1/guided-bootstrap candidate
  and move to targeted trajectory-retention objectives rather than more global
  KL/teacher-pressure variants.

### Results

- Focused pytest: `57 passed in 9.60s`.
- ruff format check: `17 files already formatted`.
- ruff check: `All checks passed!`.
- Config parse check printed: `('control',) mixture`.
- Guarded confirm64 scores:
  - carry schedule, selected/base:
    - B2 `0.4609375`
    - B3 `0.421875`
    - B4 `0.484375`
  - reset schedule, selected/base:
    - B2 `0.5703125`
    - B3 `0.53125`
    - B4 `0.453125`
  - reset plus anchor floor:
    - B2 `0.5`
    - B3 `0.4765625`
    - B4 `0.4375`
  - reset plus cycled profile floor:
    - B2 `0.5625`
    - B3 `0.5703125`
    - B4 `0.4765625`
  - reset plus high control-profile public guidance:
    - B2 `0.5625`
    - B3 `0.578125`
    - B4 `0.546875`
  - reset plus high control profile plus KL anchor:
    - B2 `0.4765625`
    - B3 `0.53125`
    - B4 `0.515625`
- Larger confirmation for reset plus high control-profile public guidance:
  - confirm128:
    - B2 `149/256 = 0.58203125`
    - B3 `141/256 = 0.55078125`
    - B4 `142/256 = 0.5546875`
  - confirm256:
    - B2 `288/512 = 0.5625`
    - B3 `259/512 = 0.505859375`
    - B4 `282/512 = 0.55078125`

### Findings

- Schedule inheritance was a real structural issue. The selected/base transfer
  with inherited offset started from `source_init_schedule_offset=115`; public
  guidance was inactive and all B2/B3/B4 anchors failed. Resetting the first
  segment to offset `0` immediately recovered B2 and B3.
- B4/control transfer is a distinct problem. Reset/base improved B2/B3 but
  harmed B4. Cycling profiles helped B2/B3 but still under-served B4.
- The best short transfer so far is reset-offset plus high control-profile
  public guidance, without seed KL anchoring. It is the first branch to clear
  `0.5` on all three anchors locally and holds B4 around `0.55` at confirm256.
- Seed KL anchoring is not a free improvement: adding it to the high-control
  branch reduced B2 below `0.5`.

### Failed Ideas

- Carrying the source schedule into the league bootstrap: rejected.
- Reset/base only: improves B2/B3 but fails B4.
- Reset plus base anchor floor: rejected; worse across anchors.
- Reset plus low cycled profile floor: B2/B3 good, B4 still below `0.5`.
- Reset plus high control profile plus KL anchor: B4 above `0.5`, but B2 fails.

### Remaining Risks

- The reset/control branch is not thesis-ready. Confirm256 B3 is only
  `0.505859375`, and B4 remains below the selected-seed reference by about five
  points.
- The best B1/guided seed is still
  `guided_bootstrap_floor_segmented_selected`; none of the league continuations
  should replace it yet.
- The guarded controller prevented bad continuation, but the branch still needs
  either B3 robustness or a trajectory-retention objective before longer league
  training is justified.

### Next Action

- Keep `guided_bootstrap_floor_segmented_selected` as the current best B1 seed.
- Treat `main_league_guided_bootstrap_selected_control_profile.yaml` plus
  `--first-init-schedule-offset-updates 0` as the current best full-league
  transfer hypothesis.
- Before a longer league run, run either:
  - one guarded second segment from
    `runs/guarded_selected_seed_league_resetoffset_controlprofile_u10_20260516_seg01/training/checkpoints/checkpoint_10.pt`
    to see whether B3 recovers or erodes; or
  - B3/B4 trajectory-disagreement audits on the reset/control branch to identify
    which early decisions move B3 from `0.55` at confirm128 to `0.506` at
    confirm256.

  updates. A second 10-update segment immediately eroded B3 and B4 below the
  raw `0.5` anchor bar.

  alignment is not the core missing piece:
  - selected seed wins much more on the same seeds;
  - same-state top-family and top-action deltas are tiny;
  - the important differences are accumulated trajectory/state-distribution
    changes such as pass count, hand/stock/waiting-room balance, and branch
    length.
- This explains why more global KL, public-teacher pressure, or short same-state
  agreement improvements have not produced monotonic longer-run learning.

  near-identical same-state top-family choices.
- Keep the selected seed as the B1/guided-bootstrap artifact until the retention
  branch can pass B2/B3/B4 after at least two guarded segments.

## 2026-05-16 - Trajectory-Retention Lane Implemented and Rejected as Simple B4 Fix

### What Changed

- Added an IMPALA-only trajectory-retention auxiliary loss that imitates the
  behavior action on explicitly retained model-opponent rows without adding
  those rows to V-trace or policy-gradient training.
- Added runtime labeling for retained model opponents from configurable sources:
  `champions`, `warmup_snapshots`, `recent`, `hard_negatives`, `all_model`, plus
  explicit `trajectory_retention_policy_ids`.
- Kept the field truly optional when disabled, so disabled retention is not
  serialized as a fake all-false label stream.
- Added focused retention metrics to `training_metrics.jsonl`:
  `trajectory_retention_valid_fraction`,
  `trajectory_retention_supported_fraction`, `trajectory_retention_rows`,
  `trajectory_retention_loss`, `trajectory_retention_weighted_loss`, and
  `trajectory_retention_logp_mean`.
- Made PPO fail loudly when `trajectory_retention_coef > 0` instead of silently
  accepting a no-op coefficient.
- Added thesis config:
  `configs/thesis/main_league_guided_bootstrap_selected_control_profile_retention.yaml`.

### Commands Run

### Results

- Focused tests: `105 passed in 3.47s`.

  - `0.06 ('champions', 'warmup_snapshots') ()`

    `runs/guarded_selected_seed_league_controlprofile_retention_u10_20260516_seg01`

  - B3: `71/128 = 0.5546875`
  - B4: `56/128 = 0.4375`
  - overall anchor subset: `200/384 = 0.5208333333333334`

- Metrics smoke:
  - run: `runs/retention_metrics_smoke_central_20260516`
  - `trajectory_retention_coef_active = 0.06`
  - `trajectory_retention_valid_fraction = 0.0794677734375`
  - `trajectory_retention_supported_fraction = 1.0`
  - `trajectory_retention_rows = 10416`
  - `trajectory_retention_loss = 0.9508970975875854`
  - `trajectory_retention_weighted_loss = 0.0570538230240345`

### Tests Added

- New helper coverage for retention loss, NaN-safe finite masking, metrics, and
  shape validation.
- Config parser defaults, valid source parsing, invalid source, and negative
  coefficient tests.
- Learner factory coverage for IMPALA propagation and PPO no-op rejection.
- Runtime mask tests for explicit policy IDs, champions, and warmup snapshots.
- Batch concatenation test for filling missing retention labels as false.
- Shared transport round-trip and pending-view tests for retention labels.
- IMPALA dense and factorized loss tests proving retention rows can be scored
  separately from `policy_train_mask`.
- Logging test proving retention metrics enter `training_metrics.jsonl`.

### Failures Found and Fixes Applied

- The retention helper initially produced `NaN` when an invalid retained row had
  `-inf` action log-prob because `-inf * 0` was still evaluated. Fixed by
  zeroing unsupported log-prob rows before weighted means.
- PPO accepted the retention coefficient even though PPO did not consume the
  loss. Fixed by failing loudly in learner construction.
- Disabled retention initially looked like a present all-false label stream.
  Fixed by keeping `trajectory_retention_valid=None` unless retention is enabled.
- Retention metrics were computed but not whitelisted into the JSONL training
  log. Fixed and verified with a one-update smoke.

### Findings

- The simple retained-opponent imitation lane is active and measurable, but it
  did not solve the B4 collapse. It preserved B2/B3 locally above `0.55`, yet
  B4 dropped hard to `0.4375`.
- This makes the next hypothesis sharper: anchoring retained opponent rows is
  not the same as preserving the selected seed's focal trajectory decisions
  against B4. The earlier trajectory audit pointed at accumulated pass/main-move
  and resource-distribution drift; this probe suggests the anchor needs to be
  state/trajectory specific, probably replaying selected-seed focal decisions
  on B3/B4 audit states, rather than broad champion/warmup opponent retention.
- Do not promote
  `main_league_guided_bootstrap_selected_control_profile_retention.yaml` as a
  thesis path. It is a useful diagnostic branch and logging substrate only.

### Remaining Risks

- The retention lane currently imitates all retained model-opponent rows from
  the configured sources. It may be too broad, too weak, or pointed at the wrong
  side of the game for the B4 failure.
- Confirm64 is noisy, but the B4 miss is large enough that this exact branch
  should not be extended without a new reason.
- The metric smoke used a small central runtime, so its throughput is not a
  thesis performance claim.

### Next Action

- Keep `guided_bootstrap_floor_segmented_selected` as the selected B1/guided
  artifact.
- Do not continue the simple retention config. Instead implement a targeted
  selected-seed trajectory replay/behavior-cloning lane for B3/B4 focal states:
  record selected-seed actions on the paired audit seeds where reset/control
  collapses, train an auxiliary on those exact focal states, and gate it with
  the same B2/B3/B4 guarded controller.
- If that still fails, inspect whether the harmful drift is caused by value
  targets or reward shaping on B4-control resource states rather than action
  imitation.

### Tests Added

- Added `python/weiss_rl/tests/test_replay_trajectory_bc.py`.
  - Covers tiny replay bundle rerun.
  - Verifies focal-seat and outcome inference.
  - Verifies opponent/nonfocal rows are not trainable targets.
  - Verifies unsupported target count and packed-batch round trip.
- Extended `python/weiss_rl/tests/test_config_sections_training.py` for
  replay-BC defaults and parser coverage.

### Failures Found and Fixes Applied

- The first direct warmstart checkpoint was strong but did not have a usable
  snapshot registry/manifest for direct targeted eval. Fixed by publishing
  `trajectory_bc_latest` under `training/snapshots/trajectory_bc_latest` and
  writing a minimal manifest.
- A guessed in-run diagnostics path was wrong; guarded controller summaries for
  this script live under the top-level `diagnostics/` tree. Verified the actual
  saved summary path before logging metrics.
- Naive ongoing replay BC during league continuation did not preserve the direct
  B4 skill. This is a failed idea, not a candidate thesis path.

### Findings

- Targeted trajectory BC on selected B4-winning focal trajectories works as a
  direct policy repair. It improves all three anchors, not just B4, and is the
  strongest current B1/guided-bootstrap artifact by saved 256 paired-seed eval.
- The main unresolved problem is not whether the model can represent the better
  policy. It can. The problem is that subsequent league/RL updates push it away
  from that policy quickly.
- The non-monotonicity is concrete:
  - direct BC overall: `0.625` over `1536` games.
  - update 5 overall: `0.5677083333333334` over `768` games.
  - update 10 overall: `0.5182291666666666` over `384` games.
  - B4 falls from `0.611328125` direct to `0.50390625` at update 5 and
    `0.3828125` at update 10.
- This reinforces the best-vs-latest checkpoint rule. `latest` must remain the
  most recent checkpoint, while thesis selection must use guarded best/candidate
  promotion. Promoting or evaluating only latest would pick a worse model here.
- Replay BC interleaving with one B4-win batch per update was too weak, pointed
  at the wrong states, or being overwritten by stronger RL/value/heuristic
  gradients.

### Remaining Risks

- The direct `trajectory_bc_latest` candidate is strong but not yet a full
  no-collapse league path.
- Confirm64 and confirm128 are still noisy enough that they should guide
  iteration, not final thesis claims.
- The replay-BC dataset currently contains only winning B4 audit trajectories.
  It may be over-specific, although the direct candidate also improved B2/B3.
- The destructive continuation may come from value targets, reward shaping,
  public heuristic guidance, policy-anchor weakness, or a V-trace/off-policy
  mismatch. The current evidence narrows the failure to post-BC updates but
  does not yet isolate the mechanism.

### Next Action

- Treat
  `runs/trajectory_bc_warmstart_b4_win_full_e2_registry_manifest_20260516`
  / `trajectory_bc_latest` as the current best saved B1/guided-bootstrap
  candidate, not the guarded continuation latest checkpoint.
- Add or run a state-matched action-drift diagnostic comparing:
  - direct `trajectory_bc_latest`
  - update 5 `policy_000001`
  - update 10 `policy_000002`
  on the same B4 replay/audit states.
- Inspect which action family, slot, move-source, attack-type, and concrete
  legal action decisions drift first.
- Next structural fixes should target the destructive update itself:
  stronger policy-anchor KL to the direct BC snapshot, reduced or frozen public
  heuristic guidance during early continuation, smaller guarded segments, or a
  replay/anchor schedule that measures and prevents state-specific B4 drift.
- Do not launch the full thesis league run until this post-BC erosion is fixed
  or the direct BC path is explicitly accepted as a justified guided-bootstrap
  B1 artifact.

## 2026-05-16 - State-Matched Drift Diagnostic and Hash-Seed Guard

### What Changed

- Added `python/weiss_rl/diagnostics/trajectory_policy_drift.py`.
  - Summarizes replay-row top-action match, top-family match, probability on
    the recorded target action, value percentiles, family breakdowns, pairwise
    drift, and largest target-probability drops.
- Added CLI `python/scripts/trajectory_policy_drift.py`.
  - Scores the same replay-BC dataset with multiple checkpoints.
  - Requires fixed `PYTHONHASHSEED` before loading models.
  - Sets deterministic torch controls and stores hash/thread metadata in the
    JSON report.
- Added `python/weiss_rl/tests/test_trajectory_policy_drift.py`.
- Updated guarded and segmented bootstrap wrappers so training subprocesses now
  inherit `PYTHONHASHSEED=0`, matching the confirm-eval subprocesses. This
  closes a manual-intervention trap in the current B1 workflow.

### Commands Run

- Focused validation:
  - `uv run --extra dev ruff check python/weiss_rl/diagnostics/trajectory_policy_drift.py python/scripts/trajectory_policy_drift.py python/weiss_rl/tests/test_trajectory_policy_drift.py python/weiss_rl/experiments/guarded_league_bootstrap.py python/weiss_rl/tests/test_guarded_league_bootstrap.py python/weiss_rl/experiments/segmented_b1_guided_bootstrap.py python/weiss_rl/tests/test_segmented_b1_guided_bootstrap.py python/weiss_rl/config/models.py python/weiss_rl/config/sections_training.py python/weiss_rl/training/minimal_loop.py python/weiss_rl/training/trajectory_bc_replay.py python/weiss_rl/replay/trajectory_bc.py python/weiss_rl/replay/__init__.py python/scripts/replay_trajectory_bc_dataset.py python/scripts/trajectory_bc_warmstart.py python/weiss_rl/tests/test_config_sections_training.py python/weiss_rl/tests/test_replay_trajectory_bc.py`
  - `uv run --extra dev python -m pytest -q python/weiss_rl/tests/test_trajectory_policy_drift.py python/weiss_rl/tests/test_guarded_league_bootstrap.py python/weiss_rl/tests/test_segmented_b1_guided_bootstrap.py python/weiss_rl/tests/test_config_sections_training.py python/weiss_rl/tests/test_replay_trajectory_bc.py`
- Final deterministic drift report:
  - `$env:PYTHONHASHSEED='0'; uv run --extra dev --extra sim python python/scripts/trajectory_policy_drift.py --stack-config configs/thesis/main_league_guided_bootstrap_selected_control_profile_trajbc_b4win.yaml --dataset runs/trajectory_bc_selected_seed_b4_win_full_20260516/trajectory_bc_b4_win_full.npz --policy 'direct|runs/trajectory_bc_warmstart_b4_win_full_e2_registry_manifest_20260516|training/checkpoints/latest.pt' --policy 'update5|runs/guarded_selected_seed_league_controlprofile_trajbc_b4win_replay_u10_20260516_seg01|training/checkpoints/checkpoint_5.pt' --policy 'update10|runs/guarded_selected_seed_league_controlprofile_trajbc_b4win_replay_u10_20260516_seg01|training/checkpoints/checkpoint_10.pt' --reference-label direct --output-json diagnostics/trajectory_policy_drift_b4win_direct_update5_update10_hash0_cpu_20260516.json --device cpu --torch-threads 1 --max-examples 25`

### Results

- Focused validation:
  - Ruff: passed.
  - Pytest: `19 passed in 4.55s`.
- Hash-seed finding:
  - Repeated trajectory drift runs without `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` produced different
    exact top-action and probability summaries across processes.
  - Repeating with `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` produced stable summaries.
  - Root cause found in RL repo: `python/weiss_rl/core/card_table.py` buckets
    traits with Python's salted `hash(trait) % 8`. This means static card
    features depend on process hash seed unless the seed is pinned.
- Final deterministic report:
  - `diagnostics/trajectory_policy_drift_b4win_direct_update5_update10_hash0_cpu_20260516.json`
  - train rows: `3818`.
  - direct:
    - top-action target match: `0.927187008905186`
    - top-family target match: `0.997642744892614`
    - mean probability on target action: `0.6530128902827729`
    - mean value: `0.06556571961705943`
  - update 5:
    - top-action target match: `0.9106862231534835`
    - top-family target match: `0.997642744892614`
    - mean probability on target action: `0.642236604980458`
    - mean value: `0.07051787068779522`
    - vs direct: top action changed `0.0819800942902043`, top family changed
      `0.0`, lost target-top action `0.047668936616029334`, mean target-prob
      delta `-0.010776285302314987`, mean value delta
      `0.004952151070735791`
  - update 10:
    - top-action target match: `0.9146149816657936`
    - top-family target match: `0.997642744892614`
    - mean probability on target action: `0.6403860206549074`
    - mean value: `0.07864233260342998`
    - vs direct: top action changed `0.07386066003143006`, top family changed
      `0.0`, lost target-top action `0.04138292299633316`, mean target-prob
      delta `-0.012626869627865581`, mean value delta
      `0.013076612986370554`

### Findings

- The destructive post-BC continuation is not explained by simple family-level
  forgetting on the exact replayed B4-winning states:
  - top-family decisions are unchanged in the direct-vs-update comparisons.
  - exact target-action match drops only modestly on these rows.
- Probability mass on the recorded winning actions does erode, especially:
  - `clock_from_hand`: update 10 mean target-prob delta
    `-0.06711340207757954`, target-top match delta `-0.06134969325153383`.
  - `attack`: update 10 mean target-prob delta `-0.07233148522097033`,
    target-top match delta `-0.0244798041615667`.
- Mean value estimates on these winning replay states drift upward rather than
  collapsing. That points away from "the model thinks the winning replay states
  are bad" and toward distribution shift or bad decisions on states reached
  after small deviations.
- The hash-seed behavior is structural. Current saved artifacts that were
  trained/evaluated under `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` are still interpretable under that
  same seed, but any unpinned model-load process can silently change static
  trait features.

### Failures Found and Fixes Applied

- Initial drift runs were misleading because `PYTHONHASHSEED` was not pinned.
  Fixed the diagnostic to require a fixed seed and reran the final report with
  `PYTHONHASHSEED=0`.
- Guarded/segmented bootstrap wrappers pinned hash seed for confirm eval but
  not for the training subprocess. Fixed both wrappers to launch train segments
  with `PYTHONHASHSEED=0`.
- Factorized diagnostic scoring initially failed on non-train rows whose replay
  actions were filtered out of the training action surface. Fixed by scoring
  replay actions on train rows and legal placeholder actions elsewhere.

### Remaining Risks

- `card_feature_table()` still uses Python's salted hash. Fully replacing this
  with a stable hash is the cleaner long-term fix, but it changes static card
  features and therefore invalidates or at least changes behavior of existing
  checkpoints unless handled as an explicit model-surface migration.
- Direct `python/scripts/train.py` runs still need the user or launching wrapper
  to pin `PYTHONHASHSEED=0`. The guarded/segmented wrappers now do this for
  their child train runs.
- The drift diagnostic only scores the saved B4-winning replay states. It does
  not yet explain which off-trajectory states cause the B4 win-rate collapse.

### Next Action

- Do not spend more effort simply increasing replay-BC strength on the same
  winning states. The policy mostly still scores those actions well.
- Build the next diagnostic around rollout divergence:
  compare direct vs update 10 in live B4 games from the same seeds and record
  the first state/action where trajectories diverge, then score that divergence
  under both policies.
- Strong next structural candidates:
  - policy-anchor KL to direct `trajectory_bc_latest` on live on-policy rows,
    not only replay-BC rows.
  - smaller continuation segments with confirm-based best promotion.
  - freeze or sharply reduce public heuristic/value pressure during the first
    post-BC continuation segment.
  - planned model-surface migration from salted trait buckets to stable trait
    buckets, followed by a fresh run rather than mixing old checkpoints.

  - old control-profile update 10 B4: `49/128 = 0.3828125`.
  - no-public anchor update 10 B4: `75/128 = 0.5859375`.
- The fix generalizes past the first few updates:
  - update 20 confirm256 remained near the direct policy overall and slightly
    improved B3/B4 at the cost of B2.
  - interrupted update 40 confirm128 remained in the same band rather than
    falling off.
- The best/latest distinction remains essential:
  - direct trajectory BC is still the strongest 256-seed overall candidate by
    a tiny margin: `960/1536` vs no-public update 20 `956/1536`.
  - no-public update 20 has the best B3/B4 balance seen so far, but not a
    clear overall win.
  - interrupted u50 internal dev-eval picked update 25 as best while latest was
    update 40; both need confirm eval before claims.
- Lower LR plus actor temperature `1.0` did not improve the no-public-anchor
  path in the update-20 short probe. This weakens the hypothesis that the
  remaining noise is mainly update-size or actor-temperature mismatch.
- The remaining learning issue is no longer catastrophic collapse; it is weak
  and noisy improvement around a strong direct BC policy, with anchor overhead
  cutting throughput.

### Failures Found and Fixes Applied

- The interrupted u50 command left background Python worker processes running.
  They were stopped manually and the partial run was downgraded to exploratory
  status only.
- `ruff check` cannot be pointed at YAML files directly; config validation is
  now represented by typed config-loader tests instead.
- The internal promotion gate still reports legacy anchor-loss guardrail
  failures on some checkpoints that pass B2/B3/B4 targeted confirms. Treat this
  as a gate-calibration issue, not as proof of policy collapse.

### Remaining Risks

- No-public strong-anchor continuation is slower because the anchor loss scores
  a second policy over packed candidates.
- The best 256-seed overall candidate is still direct trajectory BC by a small
  margin, so the continuation is not yet a clean thesis improvement.
- The u50 run was interrupted and should not be cited as a completed long-run
  artifact, although its update-40 checkpoint/evals are useful evidence against
  immediate collapse.
- Confirm64 and confirm128 remain noisy; confirm256 is better but still not a
  final thesis-scale evaluation.
- The salted trait-bucket hash issue remains. Current runs are interpretable
  only under fixed `PYTHONHASHSEED=0`.

### Next Action

- Keep direct `trajectory_bc_latest` as the current best saved candidate by
  confirm256 overall score.
- Treat no-public strong-anchor update 20 as the best continuation candidate
  and the first credible non-collapse guided-league continuation.
- Next probes should be targeted, not broad:
  - optimize anchor overhead or make anchor evaluation sampled/less frequent.
  - test a slightly stronger top-action anchor or B2-preservation objective to
    recover the B2 drop without losing B3/B4.
  - calibrate the promotion/checkpoint guard so B2/B3/B4 confirms, not old
    anchor-loss guardrails alone, drive candidate selection.
  - run a completed guarded 50-update no-public-anchor segment only when the
    user wants more GPU time; the interrupted update-40 checkpoint already
    argues against the old update-10 collapse.

### Failed Ideas

- Merging old selected-seed B4 wins with direct B2 wins was not enough:
  - `runs/trajectory_bc_warmstart_b2_b4_win_e1_20260516`
  - confirm64 overall `248/384 = 0.6458333333333334`
  - B2 improved to `91/128`, but B4 fell to `76/128`.
- Alpha `0.5` interpolation between the old B4-only direct seed and the new
  balanced-direct seed did not recover the desired tradeoff:
  - `runs/checkpoint_interp_olddirect_balanceddirect_a050_20260516`
  - confirm64 overall `250/384 = 0.6510416666666666`
  - B2 `94/128`, B3 `83/128`, B4 `73/128`.
- The first interpolation artifact failed eval because it copied old artifact
  filenames (`config.json`, `config_hash.txt`, `spec_hash.txt`) instead of the
  current layout (`config_canonical.json`, `config_hash256.txt`,
  `spec_hash256.txt`). The script was fixed before the reported eval.

### Findings

- The best current 256-seed B1 candidate is now:
  - `runs/trajectory_bc_warmstart_direct_b2_b3_b4_win_e1_20260516`
  - policy id `trajectory_bc_latest`
  - confirm256 overall `972/1536 = 0.6328125`
  - This improves the previous old-direct confirm256 by `+12` wins overall.
- The gain is not uniform:
  - B2 improves strongly: `326/512 -> 350/512`.
  - B3 drops: `321/512 -> 312/512`.
  - B4 drops slightly: `313/512 -> 310/512`.
  - The candidate is better overall, but the B3/B4 tradeoff should be watched
    before calling it a final thesis model.
- Continuation from the balanced direct seed no longer has the catastrophic
  update-10 B4 collapse. The new update-10 B4 score is `73/128 = 0.5703125`,
  far above the old public/control continuation collapse around `49/128`.
- Continuation is still not cleanly additive:
  - update 15 has the best confirm64 continuation score (`257/384`) and the
    best B3/B4 balance, but confirm128 (`496/768`) is below the direct seed
    confirm128 (`500/768`).
  - update 20/latest leans harder into B2 and gives back B4.
  - This reinforces that `latest` and `best` must remain separate and that
    checkpoint selection needs B2/B3/B4 targeted confirmation, not only scalar
    proxies or internal guardrails.
- The remaining issue has shifted:
  - earlier: destructive continuation collapse after a few updates.
  - now: stable but non-monotonic continuation around a stronger direct seed.

### Remaining Risks

- The balanced direct seed is only a `+12/1536` confirm256 improvement over
  the previous direct seed. It is real enough to preserve, but not enough to
  stop investigating.
- The direct seed was built from confirm64 winning trajectories. It needs a
  thesis-grade final eval before being claimed as final.
- No-public strong-anchor continuation remains slower than the no-anchor path.
- The checkpoint promotion gate still reports anchor-loss guardrail failures
  on snapshots that pass targeted B2/B3/B4 confirms; selection logic remains
  misaligned with the evidence we actually care about.

### Next Action

- Treat `runs/trajectory_bc_warmstart_direct_b2_b3_b4_win_e1_20260516` as the
  current best B1 seed candidate.
- Do not promote the B2+B4 merge or alpha-0.5 interpolation branches.
- Next high-value work:
  - calibrate/replace the checkpoint selector so targeted B2/B3/B4 confirm
    scores can choose best snapshots cleanly.
  - try a continuation objective that preserves the balanced seed's B2 gain
    without the update-20 B4 drop, probably by selecting update 15-style
    behavior or using explicit B3/B4 retention.
  - run a longer guarded continuation only after selection is fixed, otherwise
    the run will keep producing non-monotonic snapshots without a reliable
    automated best policy.

- The selected B1 candidate now has a canonical final-eval matrix artifact,
  not only targeted-confirm summaries.

  which is good evidence that eval policy loading, alias resolution, and
  B2/B3/B4 deck/policy mapping are aligned for this artifact.
- The run no longer shows the original "train longer and degrade silently"
  workflow failure. The selected alias points to update 15 while latest remains
  update 20, so downstream eval can use the best-confirmed checkpoint without
  corrupting chronological checkpoint semantics.
- This does not prove that the full thesis league run is solved. It proves that
  the B1 no-league artifact is now strong enough to use as the guided-league
  bootstrap baseline, subject to a paper-readiness/export pass.

### Remaining Risks

- The final eval was intentionally run with `--skip-metagame --skip-figures`
  and `--skip-readiness`; paper-ready figure export and readiness validation
  still need a separate pass.
- Confirm depth is capped at the current `256`-seed report file unless the seed
  contract is deliberately extended.
- Recursive continuation is plateauing. Further B1 improvement should come
  from a new structural hypothesis, not more selected-checkpoint continuation.

### Next Action

- Run the final paper artifact/readiness/export path for this selected B1
  artifact or wire this `selected_candidate` into the guided league bootstrap
  as the seed baseline.
- Clean the promotion/selection workflow so the same selected-vs-latest logic
  happens automatically during future B1 and league runs.

### Findings

- This is the strongest B1 artifact produced in the rebuild so far: it has
  confirm256 selection evidence, a full B0-B4 canonical matrix, metagame
  artifacts, figures, replay verification, and a passing paper-readiness
  summary.
- The B1 learning problem is no longer showing the original failure mode where
  "latest" was assumed best. The thesis-usable artifact is an explicit selected
  alias to update 15, and the workflow now preserves that distinction.
- Further B1 improvement is possible but should not be another blind
  continuation. The evidence says the current recursive continuation branch has
  plateaued, so the next quality jump needs a structural change or a move into
  guided league/bootstrap training.

- The selected candidate is strong for the current fixed B0-B4 surface, but it
  is still a B1 no-league artifact. It has not yet been proven as the initial
  seed inside the full main league run.
- Current confirmation depth is capped by the 256-seed report file.
- Promotion/checkpoint selection should still be made more automatic so future
  runs do not require manual targeted confirms to discover update-15-style
  candidates.

### Next Action

- Use this selected B1 as the seed for the main guided league/bootstrap run.
- In parallel or before launch, clean the automatic promotion/selection path so
  best-confirmed snapshots are promoted without confusing them with latest.

### What Changed

- Re-opened the main league phase because the previous paper-ready
  `main_league_selected` artifact was judged too weak for the thesis target,

  `imported_from_weights_sha256` in both the imported payload and
  `policy_meta.json`.

  - `terminal_outcome_backfill_reward` assigns terminal win/loss credit to the
    most recent focal train row in the same in-batch episode.
  - `terminal_outcome_trace_backfill_reward` spreads terminal win/loss credit
    across the in-batch train-row suffix of the episode.

  policy and entropy losses scoped to `policy_train_mask`. This lets fixed
  opponent outcomes inform the value baseline without turning opponent actions
  into policy-gradient examples.

  evaluation now applies public heuristic logit bias when the model payload
  requests it. `model_eval_logits_for_legal_ids` passes
  `scoring_mode="learner"` into the factorized surface.

### Tests Added

- Snapshot registry tests now assert `imported_from_weights_sha256` for frozen
  and explicit B1 imports.
- Runtime batching tests cover last-row terminal outcome backfill and trace
  terminal outcome backfill.
- Config/runtime tests cover propagation of both terminal outcome backfill
  knobs.
- IMPALA tests cover value training on non-policy rows and explicit
  `value_train_mask` override behavior.
- Eval/model contract tests cover the factorized evaluation scoring mode and
  public heuristic bias application.

### Failures Found And Fixes Applied

- Failure: imported B1 registry payload hashes changed when metadata changed,
  making it too easy to confuse file-hash drift with weight drift.
  - Fix: record `imported_from_weights_sha256` and verify tensor equality
    against the locked B1 artifact.
- Failure: public heuristic logit-bias ablations on factorized models produced
  identical eval screens at every scale.
  - Fix: factorized candidate log-prob evaluation now applies public heuristic
    bias when `scoring_mode="learner"` requests it.
- Failure: value/policy loss masking made it hard to test whether fixed
  opponent terminal outcomes should inform the value function.
  - Fix: value loss now uses all rows by default, with optional
    `value_train_mask` support.

### Failed Ideas

- Last-action terminal backfill improved some heuristic/control rows but hurt
  the B1 row:
  - `policy_000001`: B1 `0.593750`, B2 `0.796875`, B3 `0.718750`,
    B4 `0.789062`.
  - `policy_000002`: B1 `0.570312`, B2 `0.804688`, B3 `0.703125`,
    B4 `0.718750`.
- Trace terminal backfill at `0.25` produced broad credit but degraded B1:
  `B1 = 0.562500`, `B2 = 0.820312`, `B3 = 0.695312`, `B4 = 0.750000`.
- B1 top-action anchoring from the locked selected candidate preserved B1-like
  card choices but did not learn a useful exploit:
  - update 5: `B1 = 0.531250`
  - update 10: `B1 = 0.523438`
- Low-temperature refinement from the current p2 frontier did not improve the
  margin: `B1 = 0.578125`.
- Public heuristic logit-bias snapshots derived from p2 got worse after the
  factorized-bias bug was fixed:
  - scale `0.25`: B1 screen32 `26/64 = 0.406250`
  - scale `0.5`: B1 screen32 `26/64 = 0.406250`
  - scale `1.0`: B1 screen32 `27/64 = 0.421875`
  - scale `2.0`: B1 screen32 `32/64 = 0.500000`
- Old legacy high-B1 snapshots from
  `runs/main_thesis_exp034_legacy_oldleague_env8_u4_u340_to800_20260506`
  could not be used as thesis evidence because current fixed-surface eval
  correctly rejected their old spec/config hash.

### Behavior Changes

- Imported B1 artifacts now preserve a stable pointer to the source locked
  weights even when registry metadata changes.
- Terminal outcome shaping remains opt-in and diagnostic; no accepted main
  selected model currently depends on it.
- Factorized eval now honors learner-time public heuristic bias payloads, so
  future public-guidance ablations are measured on the intended action surface.

### Performance Numbers

- No accepted throughput improvement in this phase.
- Training/eval experiments were short diagnostic segments or confirm64
  screens; none replaced the current confirm256 frontier.

### Remaining Risks

- The current best confirmed model is still only a modest B1 improvement.
  It is stronger than the rejected `main_league_selected` artifact on the
  B1/B2/B3/B4 fixed surface, but it is not "way better" enough for the revised
  goal.
- B1 disagreement evidence shows the p2 frontier is already highly aligned at
  the action-family level. The remaining gap is likely state/card-choice/value
  quality, not simple family selection.
- The best confirm64 interpolation candidate needs confirm256 before it can be
  treated as more than a screening result, and even then it is probably only a
  marginal frontier move.

### Next Action

- Confirm or reject `interp_p2_p4_w025` at 256 paired seeds to stabilize the
  known frontier.
- Run a deeper loss-state/action diagnostic on p2 vs B1 to identify where the
  B1 matchup is lost, especially same-family card choices such as
  `level_up`, `clock_from_hand`, `main_play_character`, and `climax_play`.
- Use the diagnostic to design the next structural intervention; do not extend
  terminal-backfill, public-bias, top-action-anchor, or low-temperature branches
  without new evidence.

### Results

- `diagnostics/main_champion_hardneg_long_v1_u10_multiobjective_gate_vs_p2_self_20260518.json`
  passed:

- `diagnostics/main_interp_repair_a015_multiobjective_gate_vs_p2_u10_20260518.json`
  failed only the learned group:

  - learned mean: `0.577148`
  - learned reference delta: `-0.002441`
- `diagnostics/main_champion_hardneg_multiobj_from_interp_u5_v2_20260518_gate.json`
  failed the learned group:

  - learned mean: `0.544922`
  - learned reference delta: `-0.034668`
- `diagnostics/main_champion_hardneg_multiobj_from_interp_u5_v3_20260518_gate.json`
  failed the learned group:
  - fixed mean: `0.760938`
  - learned mean: `0.555664`
  - learned reference delta: `-0.023926`

### Failures Found

- The first multi-objective continuation attempt failed before learned-opponent
  confirmation because the controller's default seed-snapshot overrides forced
  `league.pool.seed_snapshot_import_filter=pinned` and prevented the learned
  champion pool from being imported.
- The v2 run imported 10 seed snapshots but marked all imported snapshots as
  champions, allowing the source run's own `policy_000001` and `policy_000002`
  snapshots to displace two learned champion panel rows from the active
  champion list.
- The v3 config fixed the active champion list by using
  `seed_snapshot_champion_import: source_champions`, but online continuation
  still softened the learned panel and was correctly rejected.

### Tests Added Or Updated

- `python/weiss_rl/tests/test_main_league_multiobjective_gate.py`
  - fixed/learned group pass/fail behavior
  - learned group reference-delta failures
  - reference opponent aliasing
  - simple `anchor_scores` reference JSON support
- `python/weiss_rl/tests/test_guarded_league_bootstrap.py`
  - controller can use the stack seed-snapshot policy without pinned defaults
- `python/weiss_rl/tests/test_config_loader.py`
  - multi-objective champion/hard-negative config loading

### Behavior Changes

- Guarded league bootstrap no longer forces pinned seed-snapshot import when
  `--use-stack-seed-snapshot-policy` is passed.
- The multi-objective gate makes the current frontier explicit:
  raw u10 is the best champion-panel candidate, while the selected
  interpolation is the best fixed-deck candidate.

### Remaining Risks

- No new selected model was published from this milestone. Both online
  continuations were rejected from confirm64 evidence before any confirm256 or
  alias publication.
- Current evidence suggests the next strong path is not another blind online
  continuation from the selected interpolation. Prefer interpolation/frontier
  search or a training objective that directly protects the learned champion
  panel while improving the fixed-deck rows.

### Next Action

- Keep `runs/main_champion_hardneg_interp_u10_repair_a015_20260517` as the
  paper-ready fixed-deck selected artifact.
- Treat `runs/main_champion_hardneg_long_v1_u10_20260517_seg01` as the
  champion-panel frontier candidate.
- Search the interpolation/frontier space between raw u10, the selected
  interpolation, and repair/stable checkpoints before launching more online
  league updates.
